:::info

La documentación de esta integración la escribe su autor y, por ahora, solo está disponible en inglés.

:::

Control your **Ecovacs Deebot robot vacuums** and **Ecovacs GOAT lawn
mowers** from Gladys: start and stop the job, send the robot back to its dock,
set the suction power, follow the battery, the errors and the wear of the
parts.

The integration goes through the **Ecovacs cloud**, with the account of the
**Ecovacs Home** app: Ecovacs offers no local connection. Gladys needs
Internet access, and the robot must show up in the app.

## Before you start

1. Install the **Ecovacs Home** app and add your robots to it.
2. Note the **email** and **password** of the account, and the **country**
   chosen when the account was created.
3. Account created with Google, Apple or Facebook sign-in: it has no
   password. Set one in the app (Profile, account settings).

## Configuration

1. Open the **Configuration** tab of the integration.
2. Fill in the **email**, the **password** and the **country of the account**.
3. Pick the **refresh interval** (1 minute by default).
4. Save, then click **Test the connection**: the message lists the robots
   found.
5. Open the **Discover** tab and add your robots.

### Device verification

Ecovacs may ask to confirm Gladys as a new device (the message says so, the
cloud answers code 1013 "Please update to the latest version"):

1. Click **Send the verification code**: Ecovacs mails a code to the account
   (look in the spam folder too).
2. Enter it in **Confirm the device** and click: the robots are listed.

Gladys keeps the same device id for the account, even after a restart.

The password is never sent in clear text: only its MD5 fingerprint goes to
Ecovacs, as the app does.

## What you get

| Feature                        | Vacuum | Mower | Detail                                                               |
| ------------------------------ | ------ | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| State                          | ✔      | ✔     | Stopped, running, paused, error, returning to dock, charging, docked |
| Cleaning / Mowing              | ✔      | ✔     | 1 starts (or resumes after a pause), 0 stops                         |
| Return to dock / station       | ✔      | ✔     | 1 sends the robot back                                               |
| Suction power                  | ✔      |       | Quiet, Standard, Max, Max+ (depending on the model)                  |
| Battery, Charging              | ✔      | ✔     | In %                                                                 |
| Last error                     | ✔      | ✔     | English text with its code, see the table below                      |
| Main brush, Side brush, Filter | ✔      |       | Remaining life in %, read every 30 minutes                           |
| Blades, Camera lens brush      |        | ✔     | Remaining life in %, read every 30 minutes                           |

A **cloud** badge shows on the robot card when it answers, **unreachable**
when it no longer does (switched off, out of Wi-Fi).

## Actions

- **Test the connection**: signs in and lists the robots found.
- **Send the verification code** / **Confirm the device**: device
  verification, when Ecovacs asks for it (see above).
- **Locate a robot**: the robot plays its "I'm here" sound.

## Scenes (Gladys 5.1 or later)

The integration adds its own cards to the scene editor, under
**Integrations**. Every trigger can be narrowed to one robot; left empty, it
matches them all. Common variable: `{{triggerEvent.data.name}}` (robot name).

Triggers:

- **Cleaning or mowing started**: the robot starts working (not when it
  resumes after a pause).
- **Cleaning or mowing finished**: the robot stopped working (done, stopped
  or on its way back).
- **Robot back on its dock**: the robot is on its dock or station, charging.
- **Robot error**: the robot reported a new error. Variables
  `{{triggerEvent.data.code}}` and `{{triggerEvent.data.message}}`. Perfect
  for a "robot stuck" notification.
- **Consumable worn out**: a brush, filter or blade went down to 10 % of its
  life or less. Can be narrowed by consumable; variables
  `{{triggerEvent.data.consumable_name}}` and `{{triggerEvent.data.percent}}`.

Actions (output `sent` or `located`: true when the robot took the order, to
gate the rest of the scene):

- **Start a robot** (resumes when paused), **Pause a robot**, **Stop a
  robot**, **Send a robot back to its dock**, **Locate a robot**.

## Dashboard widget

Add the **Ecovacs robot** widget to a dashboard and pick the robot in its
settings. It shows:

- the battery, live;
- the state, the last error, the suction power, the wear of the consumables
  (orange under 10 %) and the connection;
- four buttons: **Start** (or **Resume**, or **Pause** while working),
  **Stop**, **Dock** and **Locate**.

The widget uses the last reading of the robot: displaying it costs no request
to the Ecovacs cloud.

## Supported robots

- Recent Deebots (JSON protocol): OZMO 920/950, T8, T9, T10, T20, T30, X1,
  X2, N8, N10… The new-generation (`_V2`) and older commands are detected
  automatically.
- GOAT mowers: support **to be confirmed**, feedback welcome.
- **Not supported**: the very old Deebots (first 600/900 series, XMPP
  protocol). "Test the connection" names them.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Ecovacs refused the email or password"**: check them in the app, and
  above all the **country of the account**. After such a refusal the
  integration stops retrying on its own (so as not to lock the account): fix
  the configuration or click **Test the connection**.
- **"Ecovacs asks to confirm Gladys as a new device"**: follow
  [Device verification](#device-verification). The integration does not retry
  on its own until then.
- **"Ecovacs refused the verification code"**: the code is wrong or too old;
  ask for a new one.
- **"The Ecovacs cloud cannot be reached"**: check the Internet access of
  Gladys. The integration retries every 5 minutes.
- **The robot is unreachable**: it is switched off or out of Wi-Fi; check it
  answers in the Ecovacs Home app.
- The integration logs (Gladys UI or `docker logs`) never contain the
  password or the tokens.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que Ecovacs te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | Your robots (Deebot vacuums, GOAT mowers) are reached through the Ecovacs cloud, with the account of the Ecovacs Home app: add the robots in the app first, then enter the same email, password and country here. Accounts created with Google, Apple or Facebook sign-in need a password: set one in the app (Profile, account settings). On the first connection, Ecovacs may ask to confirm Gladys as a new device: "Send the verification code" mails you a code, enter it in "Confirm the device". |
| Email | `string` | Sí | The email of your Ecovacs Home account. |
| Password | `secret` | Sí | The password of your Ecovacs Home account. Only its MD5 fingerprint is sent to Ecovacs, as the app does. |
| Country of the account | `select` | Sí | The country chosen when the account was created: it decides which Ecovacs servers hold it. |
| Refresh interval | `select` | No | How often each robot is asked for its state through the cloud. |

## Cómo instalar Ecovacs en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: Ecovacs aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/prohand/gladys-ecovacs:1.3.0`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/prohand/gladys-ecovacs](https://github.com/prohand/gladys-ecovacs).

Ecovacs requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

Ecovacs es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [prohand](https://github.com/prohand), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
